one_liner: Compiler-instrumented memory-error detector in Clang/GCC; about 2x slowdown where Valgrind Memcheck costs about 20x.
what_it_does: AddressSanitizer finds heap, stack and global out-of-bounds accesses, use-after-free, use-after-return, use-after-scope, double/invalid free and (via LeakSanitizer) leaks in C and C++ programs. You recompile and link with -fsanitize=address; a runtime library (compiler-rt/lib/asan) replaces malloc/free and reports the first error to stderr and exits. It is a different workflow from Memcheck: no running an unmodified binary, configuration via ASAN_OPTIONS and ignorelists instead of Valgrind suppressions.
how_it_is_fast: Compile-time instrumentation instead of dynamic binary translation: each load/store gets an inline shadow-memory check, Shadow = (Mem >> 3) + 0x7fff8000 on x86-64, with 8 application bytes mapped to 1 shadow byte and a slow path only when the shadow byte is nonzero. The allocator surrounds blocks with poisoned redzones and holds freed memory in a poisoned quarantine; stack and globals get compiler-inserted redzones. Stopping at the first error lets the compiler emit about 5% faster and smaller code.
when_to_use: CI and test runs of C/C++ code you can rebuild, where Memcheck's slowdown makes full test suites or fuzzing impractical
Fuzzing (libFuzzer, AFL) and long integration tests where a 1.1x-3.8x slowdown (SPEC CPU2006 range) is affordable
Hunting stack and global buffer overflows and use-after-return, which Memcheck does not detect
Linux, macOS, Android, FreeBSD, NetBSD, iOS Simulator and Windows 8.1+ builds with Clang, or GCC 4.8+
when_not_to_use: You need uninitialized-read detection: ASan does not do it; use MemorySanitizer or Memcheck
You cannot recompile the program or its libraries: bugs inside uninstrumented code are mostly missed (only intercepted libc calls are checked); Memcheck or Dr. Memory work on the binary

Statically linked executables (not supported) or memory-tight environments: more real memory (worse for small allocations), up to 3x stack, and 16+ TB of mapped virtual address space that breaks ulimit -v
Production binaries: the docs say the runtime was not built with security constraints and may compromise the executable

integration.form: compiler flag plus runtime library shipped with Clang (compiler-rt) and GCC (libasan)
integration.dependencies: Clang with compiler-rt or GCC 4.8+; llvm-symbolizer for symbolized reports
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS, iOS Simulator, Android, NetBSD, FreeBSD, Windows 8.1+ (Windows port less well supported); x86, ARM, PPC per the comparison page
integration.thread_safety: Multithreaded programs supported (reports name the thread, e.g. T0); per-thread details not documented on the pages read
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — needs a rebuild with -fsanitize=address and covers a different bug set (adds stack/global OOB and use-after-return, lacks uninitialized reads)

gotchas: Do not link with -Wl,-z,defs or -Wl,--no-undefined (link errors unless -shared-libasan); final link must go through clang/gcc, not ld
Clang and GCC ASan implementations are incompatible; code and runtimes from the two cannot be mixed
Container-overflow checks (annotated std::vector etc.) can give false positives in partially instrumented binaries; disable with ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_container_overflow=0
This record's id is the whole llvm-project monorepo and the catalog already has 'AddressSanitizer (google/sanitizers)' with the same numbers; the two entries describe the same tool
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick ASan over Dr. Memory, RetroWrite or Valgrind-style tools whenever you control the build: it is the fastest general detector with the broadest bug coverage of the three (stack/global OOB). Pick DoubleTake when even 2x is too much and end-of-epoch detection suffices; pick Dr. Memory or Memcheck for binaries you cannot rebuild. It is the same tool as the google/sanitizers entry.
verified_claims_summary: Google's 2013 run on SPEC CPU2006 C/C++ (Clang 3.3 r179094, -O2 -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer vs plain -O2, Xeon W3690 @ 3.47 GHz) gave average slowdown 1.93x, median 1.86x, range 1.12x (462.libquantum) to 3.79x (400.perlbench). The Memcheck 20x and Dr. Memory 10x figures in the comparison table are cited from the Dr. Memory paper, not measured on the same machine.
status_note: Actively developed inside LLVM and shipped with every Clang and GCC; Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception, used as a compiler feature rather than copied code.
